newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Campaign clashes spark rioting in Indonesia.
newsitem.headline: Campaign clashes spark rioting in Indonesia.

text.p: Rioters set ablaze a major hotel, a supermarket and churches in the town of Banjarmasin in Indonesia's South Kalimantan province on Friday, residents said on Saturday.

Fighting between supporters of the ruling Golkar party and Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP) spilled over into widespread violence and church sources said at least seven churches were either burnt, looted or stoned.
Residents said troops had been flown into the city on the Indonesian portion of Borneo island and the situation was now calm and under control, although all shops and offices remained closed.

Police declined to comment on the riot but said the situation in Banjarmasin on Saturday was calm. Residents said they had heard two people were killed in the violence, but there was no immediate verification.

Friday was the last day of campaigning for the country's May 29 general elections. There have been widespread clashes between PPP and Golkar supporters on the main Java island, but little property damage.

Kompas newspaper said the fighting started after Golkar loyalists began campaigning before Friday Islamic prayers, enraging people going to mosques, many of whom were PPP supporters. The clashes then deteriorated into widespread rioting, it said.
